newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rumours swirl as police hold murder suspect.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rumours swirl as police hold murder suspect.

text.p: Shanghai police on Thursday announced the capture of a man suspected of killing two women and injuring 12 in a series of attacks that shocked the city.
But the media avoided all mention of the case until a suspect had been seized, despite the widespread alarm.
"I wonder if it is really him," said a woman in her mid-30s. "There's no way of knowing, I guess."
"Is it really him?" said another woman in her late 20s.
The official media reported that police had picked up a 26-year-old man on Wednesday during their investigations into 13 robbery attacks in which two women were killed and 12 injured.
The killer attacked his victims with an iron bar and then stole cash and valuables.
A television report showed the suspect being dragged between two policemen and a small pile of items he was said to have taken from his victims, including a pager.
By Thursday morning, when police said an announcement would be broadcast by official media at 10.00 a.m., rumour had it the killer had committed suicide as police closed in.

"He had a capsule of poison on his collar and he swallowed it when the police caught him -- like the KGB or the CIA," said another young woman. She said she had heard this version of events on the bus to work.
Shanghai residents were perplexed by police failure to give a warning about the killer.
"People don't trust the news organs and with good reason, but they are great talkers," said a Western diplomat.
"They often find rumours more plausible than what is officially reported."
